title: Halving Search

story.briefing: The routing table is sorted, and the network queries it constantly. Sweeping it once is fine; sweeping it for every one of ten thousand lookups is not.
story.success: Routing table indexed. Lookups drop from a sweep to a handful of steps.

description: You are given an array sorted in strictly increasing order and a list of targets. For each target, return the index where it appears, or -1 if it does not. Return the answers in the same order as the targets.
hints: The table being sorted means one comparison against the middle element eliminates half the remaining candidates.
Getting the loop to terminate is where most attempts go wrong. Be precise about whether your bounds are inclusive, and make sure the search range shrinks on every single iteration.

For each target, set lo to 0 and hi to the last index. While lo is not past hi, compare against the middle: return it on a match, move lo past the middle when the middle is too small, otherwise move hi below it. Return -1 if the range empties.
